newsitem.title: USA: U.S.'s Eizenstat hopeful on agreements with Europe.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Eizenstat hopeful on agreements with Europe.

text.p: Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat said Thursday he hoped negotiations on a series of agreements with the European Union to harmonize regulatory standards could be finished by the end of may.

Eizenstat said there had been some progress in talks on pharmaceuticals and medical devices, which need to be completed before a package of seven mutual recognition agreements can be accepted. The agreements would allow the two trading partners to accept each others testing and product standards.
"I am cautiously optimistic -- with the emphasis on cautious -- we can complete it by the time of the summit," Eizenstat told a meeting of an export advisory council.

The U.S., EU summit is set for May 28 in the Hague. The agreements cover standards for telecommunications equipment, electrical products and electromagnet capabilities, pleasure boats, veterinary medicine, pharmaceuticals and medical devices.
Eizenstat, who has been nominated to become Undersecretary of State for economic affairs, said he will testify before the Senate Foeign Relations Committee on May 1.
